This page is for students enrolled in LS100. It maps the modules onto the weekly meeting schedule. Self-paced learners can follow the same content through [Start Here](start-here.md).

:::{note}
The weekly schedule is modified each semester. Enrolled students should follow the dates posted on the course's [Canvas site](https://canvas.harvard.edu/courses/171941).
:::

## Student expectations

- Work in teams of 2–4, while submitting assignments individually.
- Expected effort: approximately 10-14 hours per week.
- Attend weekly meetings and review assigned materials in advance.
- Present at least one relevant research paper during the semester.
- Participate actively in discussion, peer feedback, and project presentations.


## Curriculum & Weekly Timeline

The timeline below gives a mental map of what happens each week — the focus and tasks, the reading and lab that support them, and what you submit. Weeks run alongside your research project, so most weeks combine learning with hands-on progress on your own data.

| Week | Focus & tasks | Reading & lab | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| **00** | Draft research proposal and form research team. Frame research questions, why they matter, hypotheses, the test / experimental approach, and expected outcome. | Research Guide 00: Converting the Problem to a Research Framework. | Project Proposal (200–300 words). |
| **01** | Work Plan in storytelling format: Background → Hypothesis → Experiment Design → Tool Design (optional) → Data Collection → Data Analysis → Results → Report. | Module 00A Guide 00, 01: Presenting Research Plans and Proposals; Computation Guide 01: Getting Started with Python. Lab — Notebook 01: Introduction to Python Programming (Data in Python). | **Presentation 01** — Research Proposal |
| **02** | Experimental Design and Data Schema: choose primary "raw" data format (image / video / audio / digital records); define data schema (variables, metrics) and a data-labeling guideline; define collection methods and success criteria; schedule data collection. | Module 00A Guide 03; Module 00B Notebook 02: Data Automation. | Research protocol with a Data Schema and Data Management Plan (DMP). |
| **03** | Preliminary data collection and redesign experiment plan with feedback from the preliminary data. Update draft of project report. Recording fieldcraft: video basics (camera placement, fps, shutter speed, aperture); audio basics (signal vs noise, room treatment). Finalize primary data parameters. Collect and label preliminary data. | Lab — Notebook 03: Data Visualization; Audio Basics / Video Basics. | First draft of project report. Data schema: structure, processing, and analysis plan |
| **04** | Data collection continues. Data extraction using ML: Develop pipeline - from raw video/ audio data (primary) to analyzable formats (secondary data). Data processing: developing pipelines to convert secondary data into tertiary datasets. | Module 00B Notebook 04: Computational Thinking & Fluency (Data Structures and Algorithms). Optional Lab — Module 00B Notebook 05: Python Classes and Decorators. | Data Documentation linked to data uploaded on the cloud. Notebook: converting primary → secondary data; Notebook: visualizing your secondary data. |
| **05** | Data collection, extraction continues. Data wrangling: creating tertiary datasets — e.g. feature clusters / segments, or kinematics (velocity / angles / counts). Introduction to GitHub. | Module 00A Guide 02: Writing Research Plans and Proposals; Module 03 Guide 01: Art of Communicating Science. | Registered Analysis Plan (why you chose these tests, model formulas, strategies for predictive tasks). Notebook on converting secondary → tertiary datasets: first draft. |
| **06** | Data collection, extraction and wrangling continue. Introduction to statistical tests: choosing appropriate statistical tests. Assessing work Progress: Alignment of research question → hypothesis → experimental design → data schema → data-collection status → Data visualization; projected timeline. | Module 02 Guide 01 "A Navigational Guide to Statistical Methods" | Notebook on converting secondary → tertiary dataset: final draft. First draft of the "Work Progress presentation". |
| **07** | Data collection, extraction, wrangling, and analysis continue. | Module 03 Guide 01: Art of Communicating Science. | **Presentation 02** — Work Progress. |
| **08** | Data collection and extraction ends; Data wrangling and analysis continues. | Module 00B & 02 | At least two plots for the final report. Create GitHub project repo (optional). |
| **09** | Data wrangling ends. Data analysis sprint: create all the graphs / plots for the final report. Update project report | Lab — Conducting Data Analyses. Optional Reading — Using AI to Make Sense of Data: When to Use ML (vs. classical stats)? | First draft of final report with all plots. |
| **10** | Data analysis ends. Report writing continues; create graphs / plots for the final report; Finalize code + data packaging, documentation, README, quick-start, config file. | Module 00B & 02 | Final draft of report with all plots. Update GitHub repo. |
| **11** | Report writing continues: polish and review the final report, focus on visualization / storytelling. Preparing the final presentation: practice the group final presentation; peer review using a structured rubric (clarity, methods, results, limitations, ethics, reproducibility). | — | First draft of the research report. Practice presentation. |
| **12** | Final Presentation: Research Question; Hypothesis; Experimental Design; Data visualization; Research Findings; Conclusion; Future Direction. | — | **Presentation 03** — Final Presentation. |
| **13** | Incorporate feedback into the final report. | — | Final report. |
